claims.text: Combined pulsed laser surface melting and rapid post-annealing will create a stabilized nano-cellular, phase-segregated surface microstructure on CoCrFeMnNi.
The resulting surface microstructure will reduce both coefficient of friction and wear rate over a wide temperature range.
The initial as-solidified or additively manufactured CoCrFeMnNi alloy has a homogeneous microstructure.
Pulsed laser processing can selectively melt the CoCrFeMnNi surface to a depth below 20 micrometers.
Microsecond laser pulses at controlled fluence will confine melting to the surface layer.
Rapid annealing after laser melting will stabilize and lock in the phase-segregated nanostructure.
The near-surface architecture will consist of alternating soft and hard nanophases.
Rapid localized melting and resolidification will induce microsegregation and self-organization in the CoCrFeMnNi surface.
Rapid controlled annealing will prevent coarsening and preserve distinct nanophases.
During sliding, softer regions will shear locally to lower friction while harder phases bear load and reduce wear.
Treatment will reduce the coefficient of friction by approximately 30–50% relative to untreated CoCrFeMnNi.
Treatment will markedly decrease wear rate relative to untreated CoCrFeMnNi.
The friction and wear improvements will persist from cryogenic conditions to approximately 800 °C.
Untreated CoCrFeMnNi typically has a coefficient of friction of approximately 0.3–0.5.
Untreated CoCrFeMnNi has elevated wear because its surface microstructure is less adaptive under changing temperatures.
Oxidizing service environments may compromise the tribological effectiveness of the treated CoCrFeMnNi surface.
Above approximately 800 °C, the stabilized nanostructure may coarsen or degrade.
Tight process control is required to avoid excessive melting or insufficient nanostructure stabilization.
